 Florida reports 485 locally acquired dengue cases amid largest outbreak in decades
 Monday, 2 November 2026, 22:30 
 Photo source: Fox News 
 The Tampa Bay area accounts for roughly 95% of Florida’s locally acquired cases, with 60 new infections logged statewide from Oct. 18 to Oct. 24. 
 Florida health officials have confirmed 485 locally acquired dengue cases this year, as the state faces its largest outbreak in decades. The Florida Department of Health says the Tampa Bay area accounts for roughly 95% of locally acquired cases recorded statewide.
 This is reported by Fox News .
 In late September, Hillsborough, Pasco and Pinellas counties declared states of emergency. The declarations allow faster purchasing and spraying, and requests for state and federal reimbursement. Hillsborough County has since extended its state of local emergency amid ongoing transmission.
 Advertisement 
 The locally acquired cases are separate from more than 300 travel-associated dengue cases reported in Florida this year. The Florida Mosquito Control Association said teams are increasing targeted ground spraying, aerial applications and localized property inspections.
 Dengue is a viral illness transmitted primarily through the bites of infected Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes. It can cause fever, severe muscle and joint pain, nausea and rash, and in severe cases can lead to dangerous complications or death, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Unlike many mosquito species that mainly bite at dawn and dusk, mosquitoes that carry dengue feed during the day and thrive in humid residential environments.
 “The Aedes mosquitoes that can transmit dengue are active during the day and thrive in warm, humid environments like those found in Florida,” an entomologist spokesperson at the SC Johnson Center for Insect Science and Family Health previously told Fox News Digital. “Staying aware of local mosquito activity and consistently protecting against bites are important steps people can take to help reduce their risk.” 
 – An entomologist spokesperson at the SC Johnson Center for Insect Science and Family Health, speaking to Fox News Digital
 Public health officials say Aedes mosquitoes are “container breeders” and can lay eggs in as little as a tablespoon of standing water. They urge residents to inspect their yards weekly and drain or cover birdbaths, gutters, planters, discarded tires and other outdoor containers.
 Most people infected with dengue have mild or no symptoms and typically recover within two weeks, according to Mayo Clinic. When symptoms appear, they usually begin four to 10 days after an infectious bite. Severe dengue can progress rapidly within 24 to 48 hours after the initial fever drops.
 Warning signs include persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain, difficulty breathing, mucosal bleeding and extreme lethargy. Anyone experiencing these signs should seek emergency medical care immediately.
